## Learning
Short lessons sound like a shortcut. They are the opposite: you watch less and practise more.

Most people who stop learning a skill don't stop because it's hard. They stop because the next step isn't clear. A short lesson makes the next step clear: watch one move, then do it.

## What we've seen
Across 12,480 students, the ones who finish do two things. They keep sessions short and regular, and they send their work in early, before it's good.

- Watch a lesson, then practise the same day
- Send a photo of your work at the halfway point
- Read your teacher's notes before the next lesson

> The best time to ask for feedback is before you think you're ready.

## Try it this week
Pick one lesson, set a timer for twenty minutes and make something small. Then send it in. Your teacher will take it from there.
